Joburg Graft Unit

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
More than 50 cases invovling corrupt officials at the city of johannesburg, that are seemingly simple to prosecute or investigate, have gone nowhere. We investigate alleged political interference.

Unique Selling Point:
In November 2016 Carte Blanche investigated claims that the city of Johannesburg’s valuation department had been defrauded by half a billion rand when an employee had decreased the values of 22 buildings – so that the owners would pay less rates and taxes.
LINK: Two years later and a case which had iron-clad reports, admissions of wrong-doing from the accused and solid evidence has been withdrawn from prosecution.
Responsible for decision making on cases is Gauteng’s Public Prosecutor Adv. Andrew Chauke. And their white collar investigative arm – the Specialized Commercial Crimes Unit Johannesburg Adv. Gordon Nkoane.
DPP: “We could not find the owners of the 22 buildings.”
Devi: “But we found them easily.”
Why not just delay it and send it back for further investigation? I have here affidavits from the building owners, and from the accused admitting bribery and corruption. Not just that – but one of the buildings is the Special Commercialized Crime Buildings – you want to tell me your own investigation arm cannot find the owners of their own building?”
At the time the story aired, Joburg City Mayor Hermann Mashaba laid charges at the police station when we showed him the report and our evidence. He’d only been in office for 6 months and he’d made “rooting out the rot” public enemy number 1.
“Mashaba comment”
LINK: Leaving business to become a politician, Mashaba says it’s been two and a half years of catching corrupt city officials – but many of these cases have gone no where with either the NPA or the police.
Devi: “What happened, why did the NPA withdraw this case?”
Mashaba: “comment – it’s not just this one there are many others…”
The city of Johannesburg ha n,/.nds over all it’s cases to an independent investigative unit called Group Forensics & Investigation Services or GFIS. Headed by EX-HAWKS head General Shadrack Sibiya. His history of police investigations is why he was hand-picked for the job by Mashaba. But it hasn’t come without the politics.
Sibiya: “explains why burning ntlemeza has publicly said he will ensure cases of corrupt officials at COJ are stalled by police…”
Sibiya believes there is interference because of XYZ , he shows us a list of more than 72 cases that have gone no where, when they have 90% (X amount) of cases at the Joburg High Court where the people have been successfully prosecuted.
General: “”
Carte Blanche then decided to see how many others had not been prosecuted - what we found was shocking. More than 50 cases with strong evidence have been withdrawn or stalled – all of them cases of corruption of city officials.
Devi: “So why do you think this is happening?”
Mashaba: “Political interference… we are DA, NPA is ANC”
Devi: “You’re saying that the NPA are declining to prosecute cases because of political party lines?” Why?
Mashaba: “Comment”
Devi: Your office are being accused of not prosecuting cases because of political interference – is that true?
DPP: “comment – likely a denial.”
LINK: I think we should go through a hand full of these cases – we’ve chosen a sample of 10. In order to do this, we needed to go to GFIS.
In this office lies hundreds of cases all scrutinized by a highly proficient team of investigators…General Sibiya…
Show mbali’s – ROR…
Devi: “General lets start with our case – what’s happening?”
General: “Mbali Maclare admitted she was paid to change the valuations of property’s. Not just that – but one of the buildings is the Special Commercialized Crime Buildings – you want to tell me your own investigation arm cannot find the owners of their own building?”
Since then Mbali has even been emailing her valuation deals from a jail cell. Show emails.
Devi: Our investigative unit has scoured 20% of the cases of the more than 50 here.


Summary:
Basically 10 stories on 1

Further information:
Let’s start with this joburg city market – what happened?
In 2015 the tender of 35 Rocker bins was awarded to MKSA holdings for R604 286. The allegations made by this report show that the tender process was irregular, one of the reasons for this was that the contract was awarded to a joburg markets – entitiy of the COJ - manager’s friend’s wife – owner of MKSA holdings Ms. Mpati – whose husband Mr. Anthony Mpati is a friend of city employee Mr Wandile Modiba – Project manager of infrastructure. The 35 rocker bins although appeared to have been delivered - in reality never were: Mr. Modiba signed 3 of the MKSA holdings delivery notes indicating Joburg Market received the 35 rocker bins in January 2016. But during check of the asset registered the rocker bins, although tagged, didn’t exist.
A lifestyle audit of Mr. Modiba showed with a salary R32k – he owns 6 properties – some with no bond , 16 vehicles registered in his other companies and wifes name – some were partially paid in cash – allegedly this photo of him with a ferarri... There were several other cases of similar fraud – amounting to R7 million. (show 3.1) – the report notes that Mr. Modiba has been with the city since 2006 and was responsible for many contracts over the years.
Right of reply
Modiba and Mpati
Joburg market
Devi: Is this man still employed?
Mayor: yes for 2 years he has been suspended – and paid full salary…
More shocking is the fact that the NPA withdrew…”The case was investigated and forwarded to the NPA for a decision. The charges were withdrawn GFIS has requested reasons.”
NPA response

IN Jan 2018 a whistleblower at Isizwe technology said 500 computers ordered by COJ were not delivered. Upon arrival, together with the Hawks, 37 Acer Desktop computers with the serial numbers filed off were pointed out by whistleblower (accounts manager at Isizwe). They were seized after Mr. Deon Pillay failed to give an explanation – documents were seized which implicated city employees who has been paid by Isizwe technology. Ms. Linda Dingane from the city, was fingered – she was paid R1,000,000 allegedly by Isizwe to cover for the non-delivery of the computers.
ROR Pillay and Dingane
NPA – “The case was investigated and handed over to NPA for prosecution. The NPA declined to prosecute. GFIS made a presentation to NPA to review their decision not to prosecute. It was established that the docket had been stolen from the police station archives. GFIS provided SAPS with documents in order to reconstruct another docket.”
Npa and Saps response

Setheo Engineering/ Setheo Investments – did both substations Eldorado Park (new substation) and Hopefield (fire damage). On March 26 2015, City Power entered into contract with Setheo Investments – yet the contract was awarded to Setheo Engineering. By 22 May 2017 in an investigation 6 invoices show they were paid up from – two of which equated to R12.3 million of irregular expenditure – Hopefield substation was just an upgrade and those two invoices were for “prelim and general charges” – but as it was an existing site, no earthworks or prep work was required (#14 pg 3) Item 15 – Similar trend with the invoices and payments for the trend of work completion certificates completed on work not done. City power employees refused to interviews, and documents went missing. For Eldorado R30,501,445 was paid for work not done. On Hopefield they found out that Setheo Investments has outstanding taxes and municipal bills, and no CIDB rating, no BEE status which is why their tax number is for engineering is actual for Investments . All the tender processes were irregular. They paid R76, 290,280 million in irregular expenditure. Setheo also sent City Power a fraudulent R14 million bank guarantee from Absa.
ROR City Power, Setheo
NPA case: “The case was investigated and evidence submitted by GFIS. The case was provisionally withdrawn and reasons provided was that they were awaiting statement from engineers of city power. The statement were submitted, however, the delay continues and FIS was advised by SAPS that they are awaiting financial analysis from Priority Crime Special Investigations Unit.”
Mayor – went on a site visit and realized there’s nothing there.
NPA response

6 COJ staff were caught allegedly fraudulently manipulating meter readings on the system to reduce bills of customers, receiving personal favours at Hilton Hotel…The company Boffin and Fundi (collection attorney’s) were appointed to collect debt for COJ - they disbanded the internal collections department of COJ for their own benefit: 15 allegations. Irregular tender allocation, no agreement , boffin and fundi were given space in the Thuso House bulding – utilized furniture, telephones, computers and network facilities. COJ did not recover overhead costs including rent and cleaning. They made R90 million.
NPA: “The case was investigated and forwarded to the office of the NPA for a decision. The charges were withdrawn. GFIS requested a reason and has not been provided with such.”
Thuso house…
Basically COJ employee Ms Nombeko, Mr. Shabalal) a, Mr. Ngubane at Johannesburg Property Company were renting out 8 JPC properties in Orange Grove illegally and getting paid rent/ toys for kids from them. There is evidence in items found at properties and whatsapp messages between him and illegal occupants. We also have his bank accounts. She also had security company pay R582 254 on security to guard the orange grove houses.
ROR – COJ employees and tenants?
NPA response

HAWKS HEAD BERNING NHLAMENZA SAID PUBLICLICY ALL CASES FROM JOBURG MUST COME TO HIM WHERE THEY WILL BE STALLED. We will not show some cases of how the SAPS dropped the ball…
Alleged Hijack property, it was alleged the monthly rental is collected by hijackers at Sylvia Court and rates and taxes are not paid over to the city. They hijackers are known and have admitted the crime. R2,000,000.
ROR?
NPA +SAPS : “The case was investigated, during the investigation. GFIS obtained the necessary witness statements. Suspects also submitted the statements admitting to the crime, however, no arrest had been made and the investigation is not proceeding.”
Alleged fraud and corruption. It was alleged that Harrison Reef owed the City R2 million for rates and taxes. Two officials of City created a dummy account called Arrison Reef wherein the R2.4 million debt was transferred.
SAPS “The case was investigated GFIS obtained witness statements, feedback from I/O in June 2018 was that they are awaiting a warning statement from suspect. Since then there has been no progress.”
Freedom underlaw?
Ground as a prosecutor… Gerrie Nel kind of person…
Alleged fraud and corruption – it was alleged that fire arms used for cash and transit robberies were obtained and are owned by JMPD officers.
ROR JMPD
SAPS: “The investigation is not proceeding and has been delayed. GFIS has not been provided with feedback and reasons for the delay. The matter was escalated to General Mokotedi for intervention.”

EX-MMC for housing BOVU received a R600,000 bribe for land RDP housing owned by COJ.
ANC councilor and Housing MMC a the time Dan Bovu demanded money from two different people for an RDP stand. Bovu used Thembelihle Trust as the conduit for where the money would be paid. The case was moved to Pretoria, where it sat for a year, but when the case proceeded finally in joburg, both witnesses pulled out. Jackson wrote an affidavit saying the reason he is pulling out is because he was paid R100,000 (R43,000 cash) not to testify in march this year.
ROR BOVU
The NPA withdrew because the tenants/witnesses withdrew – but they said they were paid to withdraw. Witnesses paid R100,000 to withdraw.
Political interference conclusion

Script:


Johannesburg City mayor Herman Mashaba has made catching corrupt city officials and prosecuting their cases his number one priority.
LINK: BUT A DOCUMENT LEAKED TO CARTE BLANCHE SHOWS THAT MANY OF THESE CASES – MORE THAN 50 - ARE ALLEGED TO HAVE GONE NOWHERE WITH EITHER THE NPA OR THE POLICE OR HAWKS.
The city reported these cases to the authorities. They all implicate public officials and contain evidence like independent forensic reports, financials and affidavits. Carte Blanche wanted to know whether solid criminal cases were disappearing without prosecution…and why. So we examined 20% of them, and will highlight these five.

In November 2016 we investigated claims that the city of Johannesburg’s valuation department had been defrauded by half a billion rand when an employee - Mbali Maclare - had allegedly decreased the municipal values of 22 buildings so the owners would pay lower rates and taxes. Using her private valuations company, she would lower a property’s value - like this building from R20 million to R3 million.

We set up a house as a test and asked her to value it lower.

Sasha: “I believe it’s 2.8-3 million, would it be possible to decrease it to say 2 million?”
Mbali: “Ya, it will cost you R2000 from my side.”
We then confronted Maclare.
Devi: “You were implicated in allegedly devaluing 22 properties to the total value of just over 500 million rand?”
Mbali: “Yes there was an investigation going on.”
Devi: “You didn’t resign, because you were guilty of actually devaluing those other properties?”
Mbali: “No.”
TWO YEARS LATER AND A CASE WHICH HAD FORENSIC REPORTS, ADMISSIONS FROM CITY EMPLOYEES AND DOCUMENTED PROOF HAS BEEN WITHDRAWN FROM PROSECUTION. YOU HEARD ME RIGHT. WITHDRAWN.
Mayor: “I got hold of General Sibiya to ask him, ‘General, I’ve just heard that this case has been withdrawn?’ then he said, ‘no, mayor, this is not the only case.”
LINK: THE CITY OF JOHANNESBURG HANDS OVER ALL IT’S CASES TO AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATIVE UNIT CALLED GROUP FORENSICS & INVESTIGATION SERVICES OR GFIS. HEADED BY EX-HAWKS HEAD GENERAL SHADRACK SIBIYA.
Sibiya: “We have the investigating officer who says we are struggling to trace the 22 owners of the buildings right here in the city centre.”
LINK: BUT WE MANAGED TO FIND THE OWNERS OF THE BUILDINGS! EVEN THIS ONE WHICH HOUSES THE NPA’S SPECIALIZED COMMERCIAL CRIMES UNIT – HOW DOES THE NPA NOT KNOW WHO OWNS THEIR BUILDINGS?
Gauteng head of the NPA is Adv. Andrew Chauke who makes the decision of which cases to prosecute.




Under him, is Adv. Gideon Nkoane who heads their white collar investigative arm.
Powell: “It sounds like what we call a slam dunk case. It should have been easy to convert that matter into successful prosecution, and it sends a very bad message to the public when this type of thing happens.”
We consulted with Steven Powell who is head of forensics at Edward Nathan Sonnenberg. As a 28 year legal veteran and a former state prosecutor who specialized in white collar crime, he believes the Valuations case should AT LEAST have gone to court.
Steven Powell: “If there was a compelling case they induce the arrest, why withdraw, it doesn’t make sense, and if there are gaps in the investigation, one would expect some further investigation.”
We asked Maclare whether she still stands by her denials.
Maclare: “I don’t have any response at all.”
Mayor: “I brought sixty cases where the general and the team came to me eight months ago asking for my political intervention. I then wrote to the provincial commissioner to pass this information to the minister of police and minister of justice.”
With 33 years investigative experience, politics is nothing new for General Shadrack Sibiya who was forced out of the Hawks to make way for General Berning Ntlemeza, who soon after, began interfering in GFIS cases.
Sibiya: “He was actually against the Hawks members pushing our investigations and he felt like our cases were enjoying priority and he wanted to put an end to that.”
Devi: “Is it the NPA not being able to do their job effectively, or are we talking about political interference?”
Mayor: “It’s sabotage, it’s unwillingness to deal with our cases. In 2017 when we had Ntlemeza as the head of the hawks, it was brought to my attention, he’s addressing his forces to let them know that the cases of the city of jhb must be brought to his attention, before anyone touches them.”
Last year Ntlemeza was booted after his Hawks appointment was nullified by the high court - for lying under oath about Sibiya’s case .
Ntlemeza: “I am a very very respected somebody… that is rubbish of the highest order.”
Sasha: “It’s a serious allegation to say that there’s political interference with the Hawks in not wanting to investigate these cases?”
Ntlemeza: “I’m a proper police officer, and no one is guiding me what to say. I did my work as the head of the hawks, and I’m satisfied of what I did, and I was not doing any work being guided by politicians, or anyone. I’m enjoying my pension… and I’m saying leave me alone NOW.”

In 2015 at the Johannesburg fresh produce market a R600,000 tender was a awarded to a company for 37 rocker bins, for the waste disposal.
Sibiya: “An approval was given to purchase upto 37 rocker bins that were to be delivered, and none was delivered.”
According to an external report the bins were signed for by employee Wandile Modiba. This CCTV footage literally shows Joburg Market officials searching for the bins, but they couldn’t find them. Several employees fingered Modiba, alleging he signed for something he knew didn’t exist.
Sibiya: “Then we investigated, they suspended the guy. I was surprised that the matter was withdrawn.”
A lifestyle audit noted Modiba and his wife owned 6 properties and 16 vehicles.

The report alleges that the family’s assets could not be bought only with their combined salaries.
LINK: SO YOU’D EXPECT HE’D BE GONE RIGHT? WRONG!
Devi: Are you suspended on full salary or are they withholding your salary?
Modiba: “No, im suspended on full salary.”
Devi: “Oh lucky you.”
Modiba: “No, I‘m not lucky because my life has been on hold for 2 years.”
Devi: “Did you they deliver the bins?”
Modiba: “I have more than enough proof that showed that I delivered the rocker bins. Because if I didn’t deliver the rocker bins than by now I’m supposed to be jailed.”
Through his lawyers Modiba denied any wrongdoing.
He says,
● the contract was fulfilled,
● no civil action was pursued,
● and the authorities declined to prosecute.
The NPA says the matter was prematurely placed on the court roll, and the city have asked the regional head to review the decision.
Sibiya: “The bottom line is the city paid for 37 rocker bins and someone certified and said pay they are here, but they are not here!”

CASE3: Desktop Computers R8.5 million 207/02/2018
In January 2018 a whistleblower from Esizwe technology alleged that 500 desktop computers worth R8.5 million had been paid for by the city and not delivered. GFIS and the Hawks found 37 computers with filed-off serial numbers at Esizwe. “Chantal” says she had no choice but to blow the whistle.

“Chantal” says she had no choice but to blow the whistle.
Chantal: “I found out that a company being fronted in my husbands name was being used to commit a crime.”
It was Chantal’s brother, Deon Pillay, who is director of Esizwe.
Chantal: “My brother received an order, after receiving the desktops from the supplier, he did not deliver them to the City of Johannesburg, but then proceeded to go and an invoice the city for the desktops.”
LINK: IT’S ALLEGED THE CITY EMPLOYEE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE FRAUD WAS PAID R1 MILLION BRIBE BY ISIZWE TO SECURE THE TENDER AND THEN COVER FOR THE NON-DELIVERY OF THE DESKTOPS. BUT HOW DO YOU HIDE THAT AMOUNT OF MONEY? EASY – SET UP A BANK ACCOUNT CALLED ENTERTAINMENT 1 – AND GIVE THEM A CREDIT CARD TO SPEND ON ELECTRONICS, PETROL, LIQUOR OR JUST STRAIGHT CASH WITHDRAWALS… CLEVER BUT NOT CLEVER ENOUGH.
That city employee was Linda Dingane.
Devi: “The allegation was that you paid a bribe of a million rand. Do you deny that?”
Linda: “Yes I do deny that. I have no knowledge of that.”
Devi: “You asked them to email you a breakdown of the amount of money that you you have spent?”
Linda: “There’s never been anything of that nature.”
She denied rigging the tender, as the decision lay with a more senior official.
Devi: “So then why did they suspend you?”
Linda: “You know what I have no idea.”
LINK: THE CASE WAS SENT TO THE NPA FOR A PROSECUTION DECISION – BUT WHEN THEY LOOKED AT THE DOCKET – IT WAS MISSING FROM THE MONDEOR POLICE STATION.
Devi: “What did the NPA say?”
Sibiya: “They nollied the case, and we made a representation, they refused to prosecute.”
Steven: “A withdrawal means that the prosecutor is not satisfied that there’s merit to this complaint, sometimes you’ll make decision called a nolle prosequi, and that’s the prosecutor saying I decline to prosecute. The city of joburg can actually meet with the head of the NPA to see if there’s any nefarious or sinister reason why they’re not proceeding.”
And thk, and others.
The NPA says the case has been reconstructed and will be revisited by the Regional Head.
Sibiya: “The city is like a milking cow! The city paid for computers that happened to be on the premises of this person and the city did confirm that these are our computers.”
Deon Pillay : “I’ve got documentation from the NPA, and the Hawks, stating that there was no such evidence to support this claim. And you’ll probably know there was never any charges laid against me or the company, it was just an allegation.”
In writing Pillay says,

● Isizwe dismissed Chantal for fraud and theft;
● He has the delivery note issued for the computers, and COJ employees failed to identify them;
● He denies paying a bribe to Linda Dingane, or having knowledge of the missing docket.
Mayor: “We’ve got invoices which we provided them, and we’ve got a whistleblower which is the sister, but we don’t have computers.”
Devi: “I’m finding a pattern here, a service provider gets paid to provide a service or deliver goods, that never happens?”
Sibiya: “Yes.”
Devi: “And then they get away with it?”
Sibiya: “Yes, it happens every day in the city.”


Sibiya: “The owners owed the city an amount of 2.1 million, now what the city’s two officials did, they created a dummy account, and instead of Harrison, they removed the h and made it arrison, and they dumped the account into arrison to clear the account of Harrison.”
LINK: GFIS ASSISTED SAPS IN OBTAINING STATEMENTS REGARDING THE ARRISON, I MEAN HARRISON CASE, AND EVEN-THOUGH THE DOCUMENTS ARE THERE – NO ARRESTS HAVE BEEN MADE.
Sibiya: “The officials who did that, admitted to having done that, we’re still waiting almost 7 months now. Just to keep the success rate of the unit low.”
Hawks spokesperson Brig. Hangwani Mulaudzi says they are engaging with the city on these cases, but the methodology and complex process takes time. He says unequivocally “there is no political interference when conducting our investigations.”

In 2015 City Power authorized two power station upgrades - Eldorado Park needed a new substation and Hopefield needed repairing after fire damage.
BOTH tenders were awarded to Setheo Engineering.

But by 2017 fraud and corruption allegations resulted in this external report.
Sibiya: “I can take you there now, it’s not upgraded, someone certified that the city can pay.”
THE REPORT ALLEGES ON NUMEROUS OCCASIONS SETHEO WAS PAID FOR WORK NOT DONE;
● R31 million at Eldorado Park;
● and R6 million at Hopefield.
Mayor: “I went to the hawks to give them invoices, 28 different invoices of payments and there was there was no substation.”
LINK: ITS NORMAL FOR THE CITY TO REQUEST A BANK GUARANTEE AS THIS ENSURES THAT THE SERVICE PROVIDER WON’T GO BANKRUPT DURING THE PROJECT. IN THIS CASE, THE ENGINEERING COMPANY SETHEO ENGINEERING PROVIDED A 14 MILLION ABSA BANK GUARANTEE, THIS LOOKS REAL RIGHT? NOPE. THIS IS A FRAUDULENT DOCUMENT.
The audit report says Absa bank confirmed the document was fraudulent. But then the NPA unexpectedly withdrew the case.
Devi: “Were you shocked when you heard that?”
Sibiya: “I can’t say I was shocked. Because it’s becoming a norm. This is a fraudulent bank guarantee, we never issued this, what more evidence do you need as a prosecutor?”
Powell: “Money trails do not lie. And usually if they lead to a suspect's door, it’s very difficult to understand why one wouldn’t want to pursue that.”
Setheo Engineering Director Tinashe Mangwane denies any wrongdoing.
Devi: “And the fraudulent bank guarantee?”
Mangwane: It’s just an excuse for them not to pay us. Also, even the money that they gave us upfront that money was paid back.”
“Devi: Yes?”
Mangwane: “Now they owe us R47 million and they’re refusing to pay that. We’ve taken that to court, and we’ve issued summons against them.”
In writing, Setheo said,
● They paid a third party to assist them with the bank guarantee, and the charge was not sustained
● All payments were approved by City Power
● 70-85% of costs were for this equipment - and normally substations aren’t built on site


They say this is malicious prosecution, as Mashaba is “hiding under a false cloak of being an anti-corruption crusader,” who has “sacrificed service delivery for cheap tweets and retweets.”
Mashaba says Setheo’s allegations are “absurd” and “without basis.” City Power “denies any debt” and “looks forward to defending the matter”.
Devi: “Do you think the NPA is willfully stalling or withdrawing, or declining to prosecute your cases?”
Sibiya: “We are of the strong view that we have a strong case and then the prosecutor will look and feel that it’s not much. I have a prosecutor we recruited from the NPA from Comm. Crime itself; we have effective and experienced investigators to an extent that even myself, I would go through cases, and then we’ll agree that we do have a case.”
THE NPA Says:
● There has never been political interference ;
● Like any other case, prosecutors assess if there’s sufficient and admissible evidence to obtain a successful prosecution;
● No case has been stalled or not investigated purposefully
Devi: “We just been told that there’s SAPS asked for a meeting with the general, that’s after we sent questions around these cases?”
Mayor: “Well, I pray that they take interest in this matter because these matters are not about me, but South Africa, about jhb because without jhb working, South African is not going to work.”

references from Insert in Show: Title Author Last Updated 09 December 2018 - Carte Blanche HD Nikola Vrahimis 28 January 2019 Script: Johannesburg City mayor Herman Mashaba has made catching corrupt city officials and prosecuting their cases his number one priority. LINK: BUT A DOCUMENT LEAKED TO CARTE BLANCHE SHOWS THAT MANY OF THESE CASES – MORE THAN 50 - ARE ALLEGED TO HAVE GONE NOWHERE WITH EITHER THE NPA OR THE POLICE OR HAWKS. The city reported these cases to the authorities. They all implicate public officials and contain evidence like independent forensic reports, financials and affidavits. Carte Blanche wanted to know whether solid criminal cases were disappearing without prosecution…and why. So we examined 20% of them, and will highlight these five. In November 2016 we investigated claims that the city of Johannesburg’s valuation department had been defrauded by half a billion rand when an employee - Mbali Maclare - had allegedly decreased the municipal values of 22 buildings so the owners would pay lower rates and taxes. Using her private valuations company, she would lower a property’s value - like this building from R20 million to R3 million. We set up a house as a test and asked her to value it lower. Sasha: “I believe it’s 2.8-3 million, would it be possible to decrease it to say 2 million?” Mbali: “Ya, it will cost you R2000 from my side.” We then confronted Maclare. Devi: “You were implicated in allegedly devaluing 22 properties to the total value of just over 500 million rand?” Mbali: “Yes there was an investigation going on.” Devi: “You didn’t resign, because you were guilty of actually devaluing those other properties?” Mbali: “No.” TWO YEARS LATER AND A CASE WHICH HAD FORENSIC REPORTS, ADMISSIONS FROM CITY EMPLOYEES AND DOCUMENTED PROOF HAS BEEN WITHDRAWN FROM PROSECUTION. YOU HEARD ME RIGHT. WITHDRAWN. Mayor: “I got hold of General Sibiya to ask him, ‘General, I’ve just heard that this case has been withdrawn?’ then he said, ‘no, mayor, this is not the only case.” LINK: THE CITY OF JOHANNESBURG HANDS OVER ALL IT’S CASES TO AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATIVE UNIT CALLED GROUP FORENSICS & INVESTIGATION SERVICES OR GFIS. HEADED BY EX-HAWKS HEAD GENERAL SHADRACK SIBIYA. Sibiya: “We have the investigating officer who says we are struggling to trace the 22 owners of the buildings right here in the city centre.” LINK: BUT WE MANAGED TO FIND THE OWNERS OF THE BUILDINGS! EVEN THIS ONE WHICH HOUSES THE NPA’S SPECIALIZED COMMERCIAL CRIMES UNIT – HOW DOES THE NPA NOT KNOW WHO OWNS THEIR BUILDINGS? Gauteng head of the NPA is Adv. Andrew Chauke who makes the decision of which cases to prosecute. Under him, is Adv. Gideon Nkoane who heads their white collar investigative arm. Powell: “It sounds like what we call a slam dunk case. It should have been easy to convert that matter into successful prosecution, and it sends a very bad message to the public when this type of thing happens.” We consulted with Steven Powell who is head of forensics at Edward Nathan Sonnenberg. As a 28 year legal veteran and a former state prosecutor who specialized in white collar crime, he believes the Valuations case should AT LEAST have gone to court. Steven Powell: “If there was a compelling case they induce the arrest, why withdraw, it doesn’t make sense, and if there are gaps in the investigation, one would expect some further investigation.” We asked Maclare whether she still stands by her denials. Maclare: “I don’t have any response at all.” Mayor: “I brought sixty cases where the general and the team came to me eight months ago asking for my political intervention. I then wrote to the provincial commissioner to pass this information to the minister of police and minister of justice.” With 33 years investigative experience, politics is nothing new for General Shadrack Sibiya who was forced out of the Hawks to make way for General Berning Ntlemeza, who soon after, began interfering in GFIS cases. Sibiya: “He was actually against the Hawks members pushing our investigations and he felt like our cases were enjoying priority and he wanted to put an end to that.” Devi: “Is it the NPA not being able to do their job effectively, or are we talking about political interference?” Mayor: “It’s sabotage, it’s unwillingness to deal with our cases. In 2017 when we had Ntlemeza as the head of the hawks, it was brought to my attention, he’s addressing his forces to let them know that the cases of the city of jhb must be brought to his attention, before anyone touches them.” Last year Ntlemeza was booted after his Hawks appointment was nullified by the high court - for lying under oath about Sibiya’s case . Ntlemeza: “I am a very very respected somebody… that is rubbish of the highest order.” Sasha: “It’s a serious allegation to say that there’s political interference with the Hawks in not wanting to investigate these cases?” Ntlemeza: “I’m a proper police officer, and no one is guiding me what to say. I did my work as the head of the hawks, and I’m satisfied of what I did, and I was not doing any work being guided by politicians, or anyone. I’m enjoying my pension… and I’m saying leave me alone NOW.” In 2015 at the Johannesburg fresh produce market a R600,000 tender was a awarded to a company for 37 rocker bins, for the waste disposal. Sibiya: “An approval was given to purchase upto 37 rocker bins that were to be delivered, and none was delivered.” According to an external report the bins were signed for by employee Wandile Modiba. This CCTV footage literally shows Joburg Market officials searching for the bins, but they couldn’t find them. Several employees fingered Modiba, alleging he signed for something he knew didn’t exist. Sibiya: “Then we investigated, they suspended the guy. I was surprised that the matter was withdrawn.” A lifestyle audit noted Modiba and his wife owned 6 properties and 16 vehicles. The report alleges that the family’s assets could not be bought only with their combined salaries. LINK: SO YOU’D EXPECT HE’D BE GONE RIGHT? WRONG! Devi: Are you suspended on full salary or are they withholding your salary? Modiba: “No, im suspended on full salary.” Devi: “Oh lucky you.” Modiba: “No, I‘m not lucky because my life has been on hold for 2 years.” Devi: “Did you they deliver the bins?” Modiba: “I have more than enough proof that showed that I delivered the rocker bins. Because if I didn’t deliver the rocker bins than by now I’m supposed to be jailed.” Through his lawyers Modiba denied any wrongdoing. He says, ● the contract was fulfilled, ● no civil action was pursued, ● and the authorities declined to prosecute. The NPA says the matter was prematurely placed on the court roll, and the city have asked the regional head to review the decision. Sibiya: “The bottom line is the city paid for 37 rocker bins and someone certified and said pay they are here, but they are not here!” CASE3: Desktop Computers R8.5 million 207/02/2018 In January 2018 a whistleblower from Esizwe technology alleged that 500 desktop computers worth R8.5 million had been paid for by the city and not delivered. GFIS and the Hawks found 37 computers with filed-off serial numbers at Esizwe. “Chantal” says she had no choice but to blow the whistle. “Chantal” says she had no choice but to blow the whistle. Chantal: “I found out that a company being fronted in my husbands name was being used to commit a crime.” It was Chantal’s brother, Deon Pillay, who is director of Esizwe. Chantal: “My brother received an order, after receiving the desktops from the supplier, he did not deliver them to the City of Johannesburg, but then proceeded to go and an invoice the city for the desktops.” LINK: IT’S ALLEGED THE CITY EMPLOYEE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE FRAUD WAS PAID R1 MILLION BRIBE BY ISIZWE TO SECURE THE TENDER AND THEN COVER FOR THE NON-DELIVERY OF THE DESKTOPS. BUT HOW DO YOU HIDE THAT AMOUNT OF MONEY? EASY – SET UP A BANK ACCOUNT CALLED ENTERTAINMENT 1 – AND GIVE THEM A CREDIT CARD TO SPEND ON ELECTRONICS, PETROL, LIQUOR OR JUST STRAIGHT CASH WITHDRAWALS… CLEVER BUT NOT CLEVER ENOUGH. That city employee was Linda Dingane. Devi: “The allegation was that you paid a bribe of a million rand. Do you deny that?” Linda: “Yes I do deny that. I have no knowledge of that.” Devi: “You asked them to email you a breakdown of the amount of money that you you have spent?” Linda: “There’s never been anything of that nature.” She denied rigging the tender, as the decision lay with a more senior official. Devi: “So then why did they suspend you?” Linda: “You know what I have no idea.” LINK: THE CASE WAS SENT TO THE NPA FOR A PROSECUTION DECISION – BUT WHEN THEY LOOKED AT THE DOCKET – IT WAS MISSING FROM THE MONDEOR POLICE STATION. Devi: “What did the NPA say?” Sibiya: “They nollied the case, and we made a representation, they refused to prosecute.” Steven: “A withdrawal means that the prosecutor is not satisfied that there’s merit to this complaint, sometimes you’ll make decision called a nolle prosequi, and that’s the prosecutor saying I decline to prosecute. The city of joburg can actually meet with the head of the NPA to see if there’s any nefarious or sinister reason why they’re not proceeding.” And thk, and others. The NPA says the case has been reconstructed and will be revisited by the Regional Head. Sibiya: “The city is like a milking cow! The city paid for computers that happened to be on the premises of this person and the city did confirm that these are our computers.” Deon Pillay : “I’ve got documentation from the NPA, and the Hawks, stating that there was no such evidence to support this claim. And you’ll probably know there was never any charges laid against me or the company, it was just an allegation.” In writing Pillay says, ● Isizwe dismissed Chantal for fraud and theft; ● He has the delivery note issued for the computers, and COJ employees failed to identify them; ● He denies paying a bribe to Linda Dingane, or having knowledge of the missing docket. Mayor: “We’ve got invoices which we provided them, and we’ve got a whistleblower which is the sister, but we don’t have computers.” Devi: “I’m finding a pattern here, a service provider gets paid to provide a service or deliver goods, that never happens?” Sibiya: “Yes.” Devi: “And then they get away with it?” Sibiya: “Yes, it happens every day in the city.” Sibiya: “The owners owed the city an amount of 2.1 million, now what the city’s two officials did, they created a dummy account, and instead of Harrison, they removed the h and made it arrison, and they dumped the account into arrison to clear the account of Harrison.” LINK: GFIS ASSISTED SAPS IN OBTAINING STATEMENTS REGARDING THE ARRISON, I MEAN HARRISON CASE, AND EVEN-THOUGH THE DOCUMENTS ARE THERE – NO ARRESTS HAVE BEEN MADE. Sibiya: “The officials who did that, admitted to having done that, we’re still waiting almost 7 months now. Just to keep the success rate of the unit low.” Hawks spokesperson Brig. Hangwani Mulaudzi says they are engaging with the city on these cases, but the methodology and complex process takes time. He says unequivocally “there is no political interference when conducting our investigations.” In 2015 City Power authorized two power station upgrades - Eldorado Park needed a new substation and Hopefield needed repairing after fire damage. BOTH tenders were awarded to Setheo Engineering. But by 2017 fraud and corruption allegations resulted in this external report. Sibiya: “I can take you there now, it’s not upgraded, someone certified that the city can pay.” THE REPORT ALLEGES ON NUMEROUS OCCASIONS SETHEO WAS PAID FOR WORK NOT DONE; ● R31 million at Eldorado Park; ● and R6 million at Hopefield. Mayor: “I went to the hawks to give them invoices, 28 different invoices of payments and there was there was no substation.” LINK: ITS NORMAL FOR THE CITY TO REQUEST A BANK GUARANTEE AS THIS ENSURES THAT THE SERVICE PROVIDER WON’T GO BANKRUPT DURING THE PROJECT. IN THIS CASE, THE ENGINEERING COMPANY SETHEO ENGINEERING PROVIDED A 14 MILLION ABSA BANK GUARANTEE, THIS LOOKS REAL RIGHT? NOPE. THIS IS A FRAUDULENT DOCUMENT. The audit report says Absa bank confirmed the document was fraudulent. But then the NPA unexpectedly withdrew the case. Devi: “Were you shocked when you heard that?” Sibiya: “I can’t say I was shocked. Because it’s becoming a norm. This is a fraudulent bank guarantee, we never issued this, what more evidence do you need as a prosecutor?” Powell: “Money trails do not lie. And usually if they lead to a suspect's door, it’s very difficult to understand why one wouldn’t want to pursue that.” Setheo Engineering Director Tinashe Mangwane denies any wrongdoing. Devi: “And the fraudulent bank guarantee?” Mangwane: It’s just an excuse for them not to pay us. Also, even the money that they gave us upfront that money was paid back.” “Devi: Yes?” Mangwane: “Now they owe us R47 million and they’re refusing to pay that. We’ve taken that to court, and we’ve issued summons against them.” In writing, Setheo said, ● They paid a third party to assist them with the bank guarantee, and the charge was not sustained ● All payments were approved by City Power ● 70-85% of costs were for this equipment - and normally substations aren’t built on site They say this is malicious prosecution, as Mashaba is “hiding under a false cloak of being an anti-corruption crusader,” who has “sacrificed service delivery for cheap tweets and retweets.” Mashaba says Setheo’s allegations are “absurd” and “without basis.” City Power “denies any debt” and “looks forward to defending the matter”. Devi: “Do you think the NPA is willfully stalling or withdrawing, or declining to prosecute your cases?” Sibiya: “We are of the strong view that we have a strong case and then the prosecutor will look and feel that it’s not much. I have a prosecutor we recruited from the NPA from Comm. Crime itself; we have effective and experienced investigators to an extent that even myself, I would go through cases, and then we’ll agree that we do have a case.” THE NPA Says: ● There has never been political interference ; ● Like any other case, prosecutors assess if there’s sufficient and admissible evidence to obtain a successful prosecution; ● No case has been stalled or not investigated purposefully Devi: “We just been told that there’s SAPS asked for a meeting with the general, that’s after we sent questions around these cases?” Mayor: “Well, I pray that they take interest in this matter because these matters are not about me, but South Africa, about jhb because without jhb working, South African is not going to work.”

(show 3.1) – the report notes that Mr. Modiba has been with the city since 2006 and was responsible for many contracts over the years. Right of reply Modiba and Mpati Joburg market Devi: Is this man still employed? GFIS provided SAPS with documents in order to reconstruct another docket.” Npa and Saps response Setheo Engineering/ Setheo Investments – did both substations Eldorado Park (new substation) and Hopefield (fire damage). On March 26 2015, City Power entered into contract with Setheo Investments – yet the contract was awarded to Setheo Engineering. By 22 May 2017 in an investigation 6 invoices show they were paid up from – two of which equated to R12.3 million of irregular expenditure – Hopefield substation was just an upgrade and those two invoices were for “prelim and general charges” – but as it was an existing site, no earthworks or prep work was required (#14 pg 3) Item 15 – Similar trend with the invoices and payments for the trend of work completion certificates completed on work not done. City power employees refused to interviews, and documents went missing. For Eldorado R30,501,445 was paid for work not done. On Hopefield they found out that Setheo Investments has outstanding taxes and municipal bills, and no CIDB rating, no BEE status which is why their tax number is for engineering is actual for Investments . All the tender processes were irregular. They paid R76, 290,280 million in irregular expenditure. Setheo also sent City Power a fraudulent R14 million bank guarantee from Absa. ROR City Power, Setheo NPA case: “The case was investigated and evidence submitted by GFIS. The case was provisionally withdrawn and reasons provided was that they were awaiting statement from engineers of city power. The statement were submitted, however, the delay continues and FIS was advised by SAPS that they are awaiting financial analysis from Priority Crime Special Investigations Unit.” Mayor – went on a site visit and realized there’s nothing there. GFIS requested a reason and has not been provided with such.” Thuso house… Basically COJ employee Ms Nombeko, Mr. Shabalal) a, Mr. Ngubane at Johannesburg Property Company were renting out 8 JPC properties in Orange Grove illegally and getting paid rent/ toys for kids from them. The matter was escalated to General Mokotedi for intervention.” EX-MMC for housing BOVU received a R600,000 bribe for land RDP housing owned by COJ.
